topic.title: Flexible Dependence Modeling and Conditional Independence
topic.overview: This cluster studies relationships among variables without requiring a simple joint distribution. Copulas separate marginal behavior from dependence, graphical models encode conditional relationships, and latent-variable methods explain shared variation. One representative approach uses Gaussian processes to let conditional copula shapes vary with the variables being conditioned on.
topic.whyItMatters: Incorrect dependence assumptions can distort uncertainty estimates and obscure which variables supply independent information. Flexible models and valid conditional-independence tests support statistical modeling, feature selection, and causal analysis, while still requiring explicit assumptions for their guarantees.
topic.evolution: The representatives progress from conditional density estimation and multivariate factorization to nonparametric graphical and latent-variable models. Recent work learns spectral representations for conditional-independence testing, linking representation error to statistical validity and power rather than treating learned features as automatically trustworthy.
openQuestions: How can flexible dependence models scale while retaining calibrated uncertainty?
Which representation-learning errors most threaten the validity of conditional-independence tests?
